title: Fix dev overlay header layout on small screens
body:
## Summary On narrow screens, the dev overlay header clips the version/bundler badge and wraps “No issues” while hiding its horizontal scrollbar. Below 768px, the header now wraps its items onto a second row when needed. The empty Issues tab stays visible, the version pill keeps its desktop dimensions and rounded shape, and the mobile header has balanced spacing above the tabs and below the pill. The wide-screen layout is unchanged. This changes the shared overlay header independently of #99002. ## Before / after Both images use the same /insight-only route at a 390 CSS-pixel viewport, captured directly in Chrome as PNGs. The empty Issues tab remains visible, and the version and bundler metadata move to a balanced second row.
Before After
## Wider screens — after The header stays on one row at both widths, with no horizontal overflow. The version pill retains its desktop dimensions and styling. **768px viewport** **1280px viewport** (cropped to the overlay) ## Verification - `pnpm test-dev-turbo test/development/app-dir/instant-insights-tab-overlay/instant-insights-tab-overlay.test.ts` — all 5 tests passed. - Browser checks at 390, 768, and 1280 CSS-pixel widths confirm that the empty Issues tab remains visible, the pill keeps its 230.96 × 24px desktop dimensions and rounding, the mobile header has balanced spacing, and the wide-screen header remains on one row. - JavaScript build, formatting, and ESLint passed. Full `pnpm build-all` was attempted but blocked by the existing Rust workspace manifest error: `default-features = false` cannot override the workspace's `turbo-persistence` default features. Runtime verification used the published canary.38 native binary.
